operations.description:
Adds IP addresses to an inbound or an outbound resolver endpoint. If you want to adding more than one IP address, submit one AssociateResolverEndpointIpAddress request for each IP address.

To remove an IP address from an endpoint, see DisassociateResolverEndpointIpAddress.

operations.description: Associates a resolver rule with a VPC. When you associate a rule with a VPC, Resolver forwards all DNS queries for the domain name that is specified in the rule and that originate in the VPC. The queries are forwarded to the IP addresses for the DNS resolvers that are specified in the rule. For more information about rules, see CreateResolverRule.

operations.description:
Creates a resolver endpoint. There are two types of resolver endpoints, inbound and outbound:

  • An inbound resolver endpoint forwards DNS queries to the DNS service for a VPC from your network or another VPC.

  • An outbound resolver endpoint forwards DNS queries from the DNS service for a VPC to your network or another VPC.

operations.description: For DNS queries that originate in your VPCs, specifies which resolver endpoint the queries pass through, one domain name that you want to forward to your network, and the IP addresses of the DNS resolvers in your network.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] create resolver rule [PATH] x amz target route 53 resolver create resolver rule [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] account address arn create creator domain exceeded exception exists found id invalid ip key limit list message name not option port request resolver resource response rule share status tag target type unavailable value

operations.description:
Deletes a resolver endpoint. The effect of deleting a resolver endpoint depends on whether it's an inbound or an outbound resolver endpoint:

  • Inbound: DNS queries from your network or another VPC are no longer routed to the DNS service for the specified VPC.

  • Outbound: DNS queries from a VPC are no longer routed to your network or to another VPC.

operations.description: Deletes a resolver rule. Before you can delete a resolver rule, you must disassociate it from all the VPCs that you associated the resolver rule with. For more infomation, see DisassociateResolverRule.

operations.description:
Removes IP addresses from an inbound or an outbound resolver endpoint. If you want to remove more than one IP address, submit one DisassociateResolverEndpointIpAddress request for each IP address.

To add an IP address to an endpoint, see AssociateResolverEndpointIpAddress.

operations.description:
Removes the association between a specified resolver rule and a specified VPC.

If you disassociate a resolver rule from a VPC, Resolver stops forwarding DNS queries for the domain name that you specified in the resolver rule.
